LINUX SYSTEM BACKUP OVER HTTPS
Each snapshot is a complete logical ZIP containing system.tar. The server stores
identical 4-MiB blocks only once per account/agent profile. Subsequent runs read the
sources again but transfer only new blocks. Insertions can shift subsequent block boundaries and cause additional transfers.

Backed up: System files, installed native programs, APT sources/keys,
Flatpak/Snap packages, all user homes including AppImages, pip/pipx/npm,
desktop settings, UID/GID, ACLs/xattrs, local applications, systemd units with
activation links, Cron, printers/Udev and further configurations. Additional
local drives must be explicitly selected. Network profiles with credentials only after selection. The backup contains sensitive system data!

system-inventory.json documents packages, Flatpak application sources,
user inventories, mounts, partition information, and capture errors.
Applications are restored during a full system restore as backed-up files along with the package database; no reinstallation from the internet.

Full restoration from Live-USB to prepared Linux target. Mount target partitions first. The partition layout may differ; /etc/fstab and /etc/crypttab remain preserved on the target. Configure bootloader/partitioning separately.
No sector-by-sector disk image and no automatic migration between distributions. Additional files on the target are not deleted.
Stop running databases, VMs, and containers orderly beforehand; a file copy of a running application is not automatically consistent. Do not manually delete server blocks: multiple backup snapshots may use the same blocks.
